label: AWS KMS (external key manager)
type: AWS's Key Management Service used as an external holder of Couchbase Server's encryption-at-rest keys, so that key material never sits on the Couchbase node. Rotation becomes AWS's responsibility, and heavy per-key traffic can introduce latency.
evidence: This method enhances security by keeping the encryption keys stored in AWS rather than on the Couchbase Server node.
Using AWS KMS can also cause latency issues if Couchbase Server relies on it for many encryption and decryption operations.
Do not assign encryption keys managed by AWS KMS or a KMIP KMS to encrypt Couchbase Server data at rest without considering the performance implications.
note: See kms:kmip-kms for why `kms:` is filed as a genuinely CLOSED axis - the one closed axis round 26 found - rather than a subject area.
